Downloaded and byte-for-byte extracted with python-docx. See the edge to `au-abs-erp` for the confirmed quote and a correction to the prior session's footnote claim.

reports.description: The audited annual accounts every Australian local council prepares — the Australian counterpart to Alberta's FIR, the Netherlands' Iv3-rapportage, and the UK's Revenue Outturn forms. release_schedule.rule: Local Government Act 1993 (NSW) s428: audited annual financial statements must be submitted to the Departmental Chief Executive by 31 October each year; the council's Annual Report (which incorporates the audited financial statements) must be prepared within five months after the end of the financial year, i.e. by 30 November.
release_schedule.note: This is a NSW-specific statutory rule (Local Government Act 1993 s428), used as representative evidence since there is no single national publisher — each Australian state/territory sets its own Local Government Act with broadly similar (but not identical) annual reporting deadlines for individual councils, all keyed to the 30 June financial year end. No extensions are authorized for the annual report deadline itself. releases_per_year=1 is consistent with this annual cycle.

reports.title: AASB 1049 Whole of Government and General Government Sector Financial Reporting
reports.description: The accounting standard governing whole-of-government and General Government Sector financial statements — the Australian counterpart to `psab-psas`, the Netherlands' `nl-bbv` and the UK's `gb-cipfa-code`, with one structural difference from all three: VERIFIED DIRECTLY (standards.aasb.gov.au, full standard text fetched and parsed), Appendix A's own definition of 'government' (the term the whole Standard's scope turns on) lists only 'The Australian Government, the Government of the Australian Capital Territory, New South Wales, the Northern Territory, Queensland, South Australia, Tasmania, Victoria or Western Australia' — Commonwealth, state and territory governments, but NOT local government. Unlike the Dutch BBV and UK CIPFA Code, this standard does not by its own text extend down to councils — see `au-brisbane-financial-statements` and the `_dropped` note explaining why no edge connects the two.
reports.cadence_note: Issued in compiled dated editions (e.g. 'Dec 2019' compilation checked this session), amended periodically.

release_schedule.note: AASB 1049 is a standing Australian Accounting Standard (originally issued October 2007), not a periodic report. It sets requirements for whole-of-government and General Government Sector financial statements. It is updated only when the AASB issues amending standards (compiled versions exist for e.g. Mar 2015 and Dec 2019), with no fixed annual release cycle or calendar. Governments then apply the standard when preparing their own annual financial reports, but the standard itself has no periodicity.

release_schedule.note: This is a NSW statute (the Valuation of Land Act 1916), not a periodic statistical release. The corpus's own url field (the in-force consolidated version) remains the correct source to check for the current text; it updates whenever a new amendment commences, not on a schedule.

reports.title: Valuation of Land Act 1960 (Vic)
reports.description: The Victorian analog to NSW's Valuation of Land Act 1916: establishes the office of Valuer-General (Part I) and requires an annual general valuation of rateable land statewide. Section 11 (as substituted by No. 69/2011 s.53): a valuation authority must 'cause a general valuation of rateable land within an area to be made as at 1 January in each calendar year' and, 'before 30 April that year,' cause it to be returned and provided to the relevant council. VERIFIED DIRECTLY: the official source (legislation.vic.gov.au) is a JS-rendered SPA whose raw HTML doesn't yield section text via regex, and the AustLII mirror is Cloudflare-blocked in this environment; full consolidated text instead fetched and confirmed via a third-party legal mirror, the FAO Legal Office's legislation database (faolex.fao.org), then extracted with pdftotext.
reports.cadence_note: Section 11 mandates a genuinely annual valuation cycle (valuation date 1 January, return due before 30 April each calendar year) -- unlike NSW, where the Valuation of Land Act 1916 requires annual ascertainment in principle but current council practice runs on an operational three-year cycle. Victoria's own valuations-process page confirms the Valuer-General has been the single valuation authority for all 79 Victorian councils since 2023.

release_schedule.note: The Valuation of Land Act 1960 (Vic) is a piece of Victorian legislation, not a recurring statistical/administrative publication. Victoria's official legislation register (legislation.vic.gov.au) shows a version-history/reprint page with 70+ consolidated versions dating back to 1997, with new versions issued whenever amending Acts or statutory rules take effect (e.g. 4 Dec 2024, 1 Jan 2025, 1 Jul 2025 - three updates within about seven months). There is no fixed cadence, calendar, or stated rule governing when the next amendment/reprint will occur; it is amended irregularly by the Victorian Parliament as needed. This is a foundational legal instrument, not a true recurring release.

reports.title: Valuation Best Practice Specifications Guidelines (VBPSG)
reports.description: The methodology specification Victoria's Valuer-General is statutorily required to prepare for each general valuation, matching the structural role NSW's Notices-of-Sale sourcing from NSW Land Registry Services plays in that state's chain -- here the connecting document is a methodology standard rather than a raw-data registry, because that is what the Act itself names (s.5AA), not a substitution of convenience. The 2025 edition (revised and published 27 September 2024) is the seventh edition, building on a 'Valuation Best Practice' tradition dating to 1998 per its own foreword.
reports.cadence_note: Statutory basis is direct, not inferred: Act s.5AA(1), 'The valuer-general must prepare the Valuation Best Practice Specifications Guidelines at the commencement of every revaluation' -- and s.11 establishes revaluation (general valuation) as an annual event, so the two sections together fix VBPSG's cadence at once per year.

Confirmed editions found: 2024 (foreword June 2023), 2025 (published 27 Sept 2024), 2026 (foreword June 2025, described in-document as 'the eighth set of the guidelines').
